Tessa Martin: @channel FYI: tomorrow we flip the docs repo to the new docs-as-code pipeline (Hugo -> MkDocs/Material) and enable CI example-testing + schema validation. This also coincides with a small SDK surface change: were introducing a unified client.call(...) API and deprecating the top-level convenience functions (generate_text, embed, rerank) over the next 60 days. Please read: https://intranet.redwood.local/docs/guides/docs-as-code-cicd + migration notes for examples pipeline
Rory Blake: Quick Q — will existing doc permalinks or anchors change? Our support KB links a lot to examples.
Tessa Martin: We added redirects for all public slugs; most anchors are preserved but some generated example IDs will be renamed. Docs CI will run a link-checker and emit a report if a permalink or anchor changes. Expect a small number of auto-created redirect entries in the repo.
Samir (eng-ci): CI details: every PR will run example-tests (runs samples against a local mock server), Python/JS snippets are executed in ephemeral containers, failures block merge. There's also an automatic snippet linter that enforces new snippet style (no long inline tokens). If you need exemptions, open a docs-ops ticket.
Nina (devrel): For SDKs: unified client.call(...) wraps the old convenience functions and returns a consistent structured response. Migration example (JS):
```
// old
const text = await client.generate_text({ prompt: 'hello' });
const e = await client.embed({ input: 'hello' });

// new
const res = await client.call('generate', { prompt: 'hello' });
console.log(res.output.text);
```
We provide a codemod and compatibility aliases for 60 days. After that aliases are removed.
Docs-bot: New pages published: /docs/guides/docs-as-code, /docs/reference/unified-client, /docs/internal/snippet-testing. CI job id: docs-ci-20260701-12.
CS-Team: Can Console surface customers who still rely on convenience endpoints so we can proactively notify them? Need a CSV for outreach.
Tessa Martin: Yes 1 Console -> Admin -> API Usage -> Endpoint Types will show counts for convenience endpoints vs unified call. CS export scheduled weekly; well include sample migration copy for outreach.
Rory Blake: Any runtime changes required for the unified call? Could this affect routing or SLOs?
Samir (eng-ci): Runtime will accept both shapes; unified call adds a small wrapper that normalizes inputs. Theres negligible latency impact but eng-runtime should review the wrapper PR for load tests. We set a canary window of 2 weeks before full host-wide rollout.
Nina (devrel): Action items:
- SDK teams: land codemods + publish compatibility patch release (links posted in #sdks)
- docs: run one final migration PR and watch CI example-tests for failures
- eng-runtime: review wrapper PR and run canary load tests
- CS: prepare weekly export and outreach template
Tessa Martin: Rolling start: 2026-07-15 05:00 PT (canary). Convenience functions deprecated: warning headers start 2026-07-22. Aliases removed 2026-09-15. If you hit blockers on CI flakes or snippet failures, ping #docs-ops and tag me. Thanks! :sparkles:
